doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Broadway pit stories: bass sax and the gong
summary: Tommy tells of subbing on bass sax in a pit; Ross tells of the drummer and the gong.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Are they? Yeah I guess Joe is. Because it pays very well, but people get nuts in there. You know you play the same note at the same place, the same second, every night. I used to do subs in the show and they’re all reading newspapers. I leaned over one day, it’s like a romantic scene or something and I was subbing on bass sax, which—
Bass sax. Did you have to borrow one?

With bass sax there’s no doubt when you’re playing, I’ll tell you that. So they’re all reading the newspaper, the conductor is reading the newspaper and everything, and the people are acting up there, and nobody cares you know. And I leaned forward to just blow a little warm air in there, because it was a cue coming up, to keep the reed wet, and went bruuuch— It was like a cannon had gone off. And another highlight.

That reminds me of the drummer in England, it’s a famous story, with the gong, the guy, he’s drunk and he’s in the pit in a Broadway show, but in London you know he rouses out of a stupor and hits this giant gong, you know, right in the wrong place. And he looks around and everybody’s just in shock. So he didn’t know what to do, he says, “Dinner is served.” That’s a famous tale. Everybody knows that one.
